what_it_does: Quantum computers need to be programmed in a specialized language that describes quantum circuits — sequences of operations on quantum bits (qubits). Large language models (LLMs, the same kind of AI behind chatbots) have been explored as tools to help write this code automatically, but they tend to produce quantum programs that are logically incorrect or not resilient to the errors that real quantum hardware constantly introduces. Techniques that work well for ordinary code generation — like chain-of-thought prompting (asking the AI to reason step by step) or retrieval-augmented generation (letting the AI look up relevant examples) — do not transfer cleanly to quantum circuits without domain-specific adjustments. This paper proposes a multi-agent framework where several specialized AI agents each focus on a different aspect of getting the quantum code right: one handles quantum error correction (a technique for detecting and fixing the inevitable errors that arise on quantum hardware), another handles circuit construction, and so on. A semantic analysis step checks the output across multiple passes to catch errors before the code is used.
